title: Equative Predicate
definition: A [term:predicate] that asserts the identity of two referring expressions — that a and b refer to the same entity (a = b). This differs from a [term:classification-predicate], which places a into a class. Equative predicates are typically realized by juxtaposition, a [term:copula], or a [term:verbless-clause]. The classic example is 'The morning star is the evening star', where both NPs pick out the same object.

examples.translation: The morning star is the evening star.
examples.notes: Both NPs refer to the same entity (Venus). This is identity (a = b), not class membership.
Juxtaposition strategy with no overt copula in the present tense. Word order (Учитель first) signals the predicate NP as definite/identified.
